craft_claim: Detached narration lowers emotional transportation; low transportation predicts reduced empathy and disengagement, while high transportation predicts its increase.

supporting_evidence.note: Transportation is defined as absorption entailing imagery, affect, and attentional focus; more transported readers showed stronger story-consistent beliefs and fewer detected false notes, establishing affect as part of engagement.
Fiction readers who were not emotionally transported showed lower empathy after one week, while highly transported readers showed higher empathy; the effect was specific to emotional transportation.

counterevidence.note: Foregrounding can evoke feeling even in stylistically spare texts, so detachment is not guaranteed to produce low transportation if specific details are foregrounded.

exceptions: Short documentary or informational texts whose purpose is not transportive identification.
